summary: Painter Hill lookout in Roxbury: a 62 ft tower with observers in 1951, 1956 and 1960 under the state fire service; no source says what the site is like now.

events.note: Observer on duty during the fire season; the 1951 item describes a veteran of two seasons living in a cabin at the tower base
Mrs. Willard Vaill of Warren returned as observer for her third season

corrections.why: The 1951 item gives the tower as 62 feet high, and the cached page text has no 100-foot figure. The record's 30.5 m equals 100 ft, which matches an unexplained height_ft of 100 in our source catalog entry for this page.
Stray capitals in the record name; the page itself writes Roxbury.

notes_for_editor: One source only: a compiled Forest Lookouts page quoting three newspaper items (The News-Times 1951 and 1956, The Portsmouth Post 1960). No build date, no fate and no status today appear in any source, so the story stops at 1960 and says no source describes the site now. Observer names vary inside the sources: the 1951 item has both Grover and Glover, and the 1956 and 1960 items spell it Vaill and Vaille; the story names only the 1956 and 1960 observers. Elevation conflict: the 1951 item gives 1,162 ft and a 1,100 ft ridge; the record's 318 m fits neither, and it is not corrected here. The 30.5 m height is a correction for a human to check. Two web searches found no other record of this tower.
